header: Problem 3: Bi-Ion Removal Battery. A bi-ion removal battery (BDI) can intercalate cations and anions from seawater into crystalline phases analogous to those in lithium-ion batteries and store them through conversion reactions in the cathode and anode, enabling efficient seawater desalination with high ion-removal capacity and high charge efficiency. Studies show that a $\mathrm{NaBi_3O_4Cl_2}$ electrode can simultaneously remove $\mathrm{Na^+}$ and $\mathrm{Cl^-}$ from seawater.

header_images.description: On the left is a stacked structure of red blocks. Following the process indicated by the blue arrow “$\mathrm{-Na^+, -Cl^-}$,” it becomes the central stacked structure of red and orange blocks. The process indicated by the red arrow “$\mathrm{+Na^+, +Cl^-}$” then converts it to the structure on the right, composed of red and blue blocks. A further process indicated by the blue arrow “$\mathrm{-Na^+, -Cl^-}$” returns it to the central structure. The legend identifies red blocks as $\mathrm{NaBi_3O_4Cl_2}$, blue blocks as substance X, and orange blocks as $\mathrm{Bi}$.
